LESSON: READIN G 2.2.1 EXTENSIVE SIGN READING:

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.2: Readin g 2.2.1 Extensive Sign reading:
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Readin g 2.2.1 Extensive Sign reading:, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 10 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why should one carefully select the text to read? 2 How do we select a reading text?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Readin g 2.2.1 Extensive Sign reading: together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to Learn-The learner learns independently as they select a suitable text from a collection of online/offline

newspapers, magazines and periodicals with information on the environment.

● Citizenship: The learner engages effectively with others as they relate the information from a text to events, persons and

places in real life.

Values:
● Patriotism: The learner exhibits honesty as they prepare and compare reading logs with peers.

● Integrity: The learner has self-discipline as they preview varied texts such as online/offline newspapers, magazines and

periodicals, novels, collections of narratives among others.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Sign Language Dictionary or Apps, English dictionary, online and offline magazines, newspapers, periodicals, novels, Charts

and Posters, Flashcards, Adapted course books.
